subject: ecce
title: ECCE Policies, Schemes and Programmes in India
meta: Lesson practice set · Question types of the April 2026 NIOS paper

Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

Survival, health, nutrition, development, education, protection and participation

Shaping health systems: investment in health and organisation of health care services

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark (match the columns, true/false, fill in the blanks or one-word answers).

questions.q: State True or False: (i) The Rajiv Gandhi National Crèche Scheme for the Children of Working Mothers aims to establish crèches and provide quality day-care facilities for children of working mothers. (ii) Samagra Shiksha Abhiyan encompasses education extending from pre-school to degree level.
questions.answer: (i) True. (ii) False — it covers pre-school to class 12.
questions.note: April 2024 also asked: 'The National ECCE Curriculum Framework aims to promote quality and excellence in early childhood care and education' — True.

questions.q: State True or False: (i) The Mid Day Meal Scheme, launched in 1995, covers children of primary classes only. (ii) The Integrated Child Protection Scheme (2009) aims at building a protective environment for children by providing nutritional support.
questions.answer: (i) False — it was extended to upper primary classes (VI–VIII) in 2007. (ii) False — it builds a protective environment for children in difficult circumstances; it is not a nutrition scheme.

questions.q: Answer in one word or phrase: (i) Which national plan for children aims to ensure all children their right to survival, dignity, health, nutrition, education, development, protection and participation? (ii) What is the focus of the National Policy on Education (NPE), 1986 in ECCE?
questions.answer: (i) The National Plan of Action for Children (NPAC), 2016. (ii) Overall development of young children through child-centred, play-based ECCE that strengthens primary education.
questions.note: Part (i) was asked in April 2026 and part (ii) in October 2024.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (i) The National Plan of Action for Children, 2016 focuses on reaching and serving the ________. (ii) POSHAN Abhiyan aims at a malnutrition-free India by ________.

Fill in the blanks: (i) The National Policy for Children declared children a '________' for the nation. (ii) The India Newborn Action Plan (2014) aims to reduce preventable newborn deaths and ________.

Match: (a) Janani Suraksha Yojana (b) Padhe Bharat Badhe Bharat — (i) Foundational literacy and numeracy in classes I and II (ii) Institutional delivery among poor pregnant women (iii) Crèches for working mothers
Match: (a) Mid Day Meal Scheme (b) Samagra Shiksha Abhiyan — (i) 1995 (ii) 2018 (iii) 1975

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: What do you mean by a curriculum framework? Comment on the National Curriculum Framework (NCF), 2005.
questions.answer: A curriculum framework is a comprehensive, organised set of guidelines on what and how children at a stage should learn, including assessment, to reach the desired outcomes. NCF 2005, prepared by NCERT, asks that young children get care and experiences for holistic development and recommends a play-based, developmentally appropriate ECCE as preparation for school.

questions.q: Name the six services provided under the ICDS scheme.
questions.answer: Supplementary nutrition; pre-school non-formal education; nutrition and health education; immunisation; health check-up; and referral services.

questions.q: What is the National ECCE Curriculum Framework, 2013?
questions.answer: A comprehensive guiding document to promote quality and excellence in ECCE across India. It aims at rich early stimulation and quality learning experiences from birth to the pre-primary years, holistic development, an enabling environment based on children's needs, and the involvement of parents, family and community.

questions.q: What is the focus of the National Policy on Education (NPE), 1986 regarding ECCE?
questions.answer: It sees ECCE as a support for primary education and for human resource development, focusing on children's overall development. It stresses a child-centred, play-based programme, discourages formal methods and early teaching of the 3Rs, and asks for community involvement.

questions.q: What is the aim of Rashtriya Bal Swasthya Karyakram (RBSK)?
questions.answer: Under the National Health Mission, RBSK gives child health screening and early intervention services: early detection and management of 30 conditions in children under 18, grouped as the 4Ds — defects at birth, diseases, deficiencies and developmental delays including disabilities — to reduce disability and improve quality of life.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Why does the government need to take initiatives for ECCE?
questions.answer: Survival and development of children depend on what is planned for them, and every child must have access to healthy development and learning in a safe environment. Families alone, especially poor ones, cannot ensure nutrition, health care, protection and preschool education. The Government, a key stakeholder and signatory to child-rights conventions, must ensure children's rights to survival, development, protection and participation (Article 39), so it frames policies such as NPC and the ECCE Policy and runs schemes like ICDS and MDMS.

questions.q: Describe the objectives of the ICDS scheme.
questions.answer: ICDS (1975) aims to: improve the nutritional and health status of children of 0–6 years; lay the foundation for proper psychological, physical and social development; reduce mortality, morbidity, malnutrition and school dropout; coordinate policy and implementation among departments for child development; and enhance the mother's capability to look after the child's health and nutrition through nutrition and health education.

questions.q: What is the National ECCE Policy, 2013? State its vision and key areas.
questions.answer: Approved in 2013, it commits to universal access to quality early childhood education for all children under six and includes the National ECCE Curriculum Framework and Quality Standards. Vision: holistic development and active learning capacity of all children below six through free, universal, inclusive, equitable, joyful and contextualised opportunities. Key areas: access with equity and inclusion, quality, capacity building, research and documentation, and advocacy. It gives top priority to strengthening families to care for children.

questions.q: Briefly explain the various service providers of ECCE.
questions.answer: Government sector: ICDS (1975), one of the world's largest ECCE programmes, through anganwadi centres giving a stimulating environment. Private sector: stand-alone and self-owned preschools and franchises, spreading even to rural areas; quality varies and needs regulation. Non-governmental sector: trusts, societies and religious groups funded by government and international agencies; their outreach varies. All must follow the state's norms and be harmonised.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: List the major policies and plans related to ECCE in India and explain any three.
questions.answer: Policies and plans: NPE 1986; National Nutrition Policy 1993; NPC 1974/2013; National ECCE Policy 2013; National Health Mission 2013; India Newborn Action Plan 2014; SDG 4.2; NPAC 2016; National Health Policy 2017; POSHAN Abhiyan 2018. (1) NPE 1986: ECCE strengthens primary education; child-centred, play-based; no formal 3Rs; community involvement. (2) National ECCE Policy 2013: universal access to quality ECCE for under-sixes; vision of holistic development and active learning capacity through free, universal, inclusive, equitable, joyful and contextualised opportunities; includes the Curriculum Framework and Quality Standards. (3) NPAC 2016: 'Last Child First' — priority to the most vulnerable; rights to survival, dignity, health, nutrition, education, development, protection and participation; framework for state plans.

questions.q: Describe any five programmes and schemes of the Government of India for the welfare of young children.
questions.answer: (1) ICDS, 1975: children of 0–6 and pregnant and lactating mothers; supplementary nutrition, pre-school education, nutrition and health education, immunisation, health check-up and referral through anganwadis. (2) Mid Day Meal Scheme, 1995: meals in primary (and from 2007 upper primary) classes to improve nutrition, enrolment and attendance. (3) Janani Suraksha Yojana, 2005: institutional delivery among poor women to cut maternal and neonatal deaths; JSSK (2011) gives free, cashless care. (4) RBSK: screening and early intervention for the 4Ds. (5) ICPS, 2009: protective environment for children in difficult circumstances. (6) Samagra Shiksha, 2018: pre-school to class 12. (7) Rajiv Gandhi National Crèche Scheme and the crèche guidelines under the Maternity Benefit Act, 2017.
